title: Bombay HC: Using a Credit Card Can Bind You to Its Arbitration Clause Even Without a Signed Application
case_name: Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited v. Maulin Niranjan Patel & Connected Matters
citation: Arbitration Application (L) No. 25878 of 2026 and connected applications; order dated 4 November 2026 (Justice Amit Borkar)
card_summary: Kotak Mahindra Bank sought an arbitrator against four cardholders, including Maulin Niranjan Patel, who argued no arbitration agreement existed since their forms carried no signature. Justice Amit Borkar held the Cardholder Agreement recognised other ways of accepting its terms, including card use itself, and referred all four disputes to a sole arbitrator on a prima facie basis.
card_tip: Using a credit card, not just signing its application, can bind a cardholder to the Cardholder Agreement's terms, including its arbitration clause, so read those terms before activating or using the card.
verification_notes: The parties, the four connected applications, Justice Amit Borkar's finding that card use can itself show acceptance of the Cardholder Agreement's terms including its arbitration clause, the reference of all four disputes to a sole arbitrator, and the 4 November 2026 date are consistent across the Verdictum and LiveLawBiz reports seen in this run, with Oquilia's two pieces corroborating the same holding. This is a Section 11 arbitrator-appointment order, so the court's findings are prima facie and do not finally decide whether the arbitration agreement binds the respondents. The order text itself was not opened; only secondary reports were available on this run.
